$comment: Generated by `npm run plugin:tools` from lib/mcp/registry.ts in the Brollss app repository. Do not edit by hand.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Who this connection edits as: the account email, its plan, its credits, and what this server may spend. On this local server nothing is paid: every tool is free and the process cannot reach a paid model (paidCalls stays at 0).

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: The account's projects (its own and those shared with it), most recently CREATED first: id, name, createdAt, updatedAt, length, format, whether it has a transcript and a video, your role. Copies often share a name: createdAt tells them apart. Filter by name with query.

tools.name: get_project_state
tools.description: Open a project and read its state: format, montage length, transcript size and how much is cut, every B-roll and every zoom with its id and its moment (word keys fromKey/toKey, which the gestures take, and montage seconds, which look_at_montage takes), captions, music, silences, and editRevision (give it back as expectedRevision when you write). Read it first, and again after a conflict.

projectId.description: The project id (from list_projects or clone_project).

tools.name: clone_project
tools.description: Copy a project you own into a new project of the same account (transcript, cuts, B-rolls, zooms, video), and return the new id. Edit the clone, not the original, unless the creator asked otherwise. Counts against the plan's number of projects.

projectId.description: The project id (from list_projects or clone_project).

name.description: The clone's name (default: the original's name plus « (MCP) »).

tools.name: create_checkpoint
tools.description: Save a checkpoint of the project now, named « MCP · <label> », that the creator can restore from the Studio. One is saved for you before your first write on each project; save another before a risky series of gestures. At most 8 MCP checkpoints are kept per project.

projectId.description: The project id (from list_projects or clone_project).

tools.name: get_editing_guide
tools.description: The editing guide: how to edit a video in Brollss with THESE tools, the style guides (pass style: face-camera, tutoriel-ecran, podcast-deux-voix or presentation-diapositives, the one that fits the video), the chapters of the editing craft (pass topic), and, with projectId, the creator's standing instructions (style, preferences). Read it before the first edit.

style.description: A style guide id: face-camera, tutoriel-ecran, podcast-deux-voix, presentation-diapositives.

topic.description: A chapter slug from the list, e.g. talking-head-pacing, zoom-usage, silences-and-fillers.

projectId.description: The project id (from list_projects or clone_project).

tools.name: import_media
tools.description:
Create a new project from a video or audio file, the way the app's import does it, and return at once job_id, project_id and project_url. One source:
- add_media (direct upload): {"<file name>": {"content_type": "video/mp4", "file_size": <bytes>}}. The result gives upload_urls[<file name>] = {upload_url, asset_id, headers}: PUT the raw bytes of the file to upload_url with the header Content-Type: application/octet-stream (no form, no encoding); the size must equal file_size, and the address works once. If the PUT fails, call report_upload_status with status failed.
- add_media with {"<name>": {"url": "https://..."}}, or url: a direct link to a media file (not a page that plays one).
- path: an absolute path to a file, or to a folder (with file naming the one to take), ONLY on the local server; the original is copied, never moved.
Then call wait_for_job with job_id: the server transcribes the voice (on its own machine or its own transcription worker, never a third party) and puts the transcript, the video, an editing proxy and a poster in the project. Then get_project_state on project_id and edit. The plan's limits apply exactly as in the app: number of projects, file size. Free: no credit. Never import again because a wait timed out: call wait_for_job again.

project_name.description: The project's name (default: the file name).

add_media.description: Exactly one entry: the file name, and either {content_type, file_size} for a direct upload or {url}.

content_type.description: The file's MIME type, e.g. video/mp4.

file_size.description: The exact size in bytes; the upload must match it.

url.description: A direct link to the media file.

path.description: Local server only: an absolute path to the file, or to a folder that holds it.

url.description: A direct http(s) link to a video or audio file.

path.description: Local server only: an absolute path to a media file, or to a folder that holds it.

file.description: With path on a folder holding several media files: the name (or part of the name) of the one to import.

format.description: The output format (default: the account's preferred one).

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: Where an import stands, now, without waiting: phase (uploading, copying, transcribing, delivering, ready, failed), progress {label, percent}, the step, the last log lines, the error in plain words when it failed, and the project once ready. wait_for_job waits.

tools.name: wait_for_job
tools.description: Wait for an import, up to wait_seconds (local server: default 600, at most 1800; hosted: default 120, at most 300), and return its state as get_job does. done: true when it is ready (then edit project_id) or failed (the error says why). Still running when the wait ends (timed_out: true): call wait_for_job again. Never import the file again because of a timeout: that would make a second project.

tools.name: report_upload_status
tools.description: Say how a direct upload went: status failed (with error) when the PUT to upload_url did not succeed, so the import stops cleanly instead of waiting; status uploaded is optional (wait_for_job notices the file by itself). To retry a failed upload, call import_media again.

media_id.description: The file's key in upload_urls (the name given in add_media).

tools.name: transcript_outline
tools.description: The outline of the WHOLE video: blocks of about 30 to 60 s with their time range, word keys, sentence count and first words. Cheap. Use it to plan the video; then read a block with read_transcript.

projectId.description: The project id (from list_projects or clone_project).

blockSec.description: Target length of a block in seconds (default 45).

tools.name: read_transcript
tools.description: Read the transcript in order, with a cursor: up to maxSentences sentences from a time (m:ss or seconds) or a word key, each as [m:ss] (first key..last key) text. The result gives `next`, where to continue, and what you have read of the whole video so far. A passage you already read is not sent again while the transcript is unchanged: write what matters in your notebook as you read.

projectId.description: The project id (from list_projects or clone_project).

from.description: Where to start, montage time: "1:20" or 80. Default: the start of the video.

fromKey.description: Or start at the sentence holding this word key.

again.description: true to get a passage you already read sent again, only when you really lost it.

tools.name: search_transcript
tools.description: Find where an exact word or phrase is spoken. Returns unit ids, times, the first word key and a little context.

projectId.description: The project id (from list_projects or clone_project).

tools.name: find_hesitations
tools.description: Deterministically detect hesitations, by kind: `filler` (euh, um…), `repeat` (an immediate repeat), `restart` (a multi-word restart), `false_start` (an abandoned start). Returns candidates with their word keys and context, and the PAUSES the viewer hears longer than pauseOverSec (default 1 s). Nothing is cut: cut what deserves it with strike_words (fromKey/toKey from the candidate's keys), after reading the sentence around it. set_silences shortens every long pause at once.

tools.name: strike_words
tools.description: Cut ONE named passage of words the user points at (a phrase, a sentence). `cutMode` carries the two transcript-panel variants: omit it (or "remove") to take the words out of the script, "gap" to keep their duration as a black/silent gap. `fromKey`/`toKey` are word keys (segment:word, e.g. 16:2) copied from the firstKey/lastKey of read_transcript or search_transcript; a unit id such as s18 is not a key. This is the tool for "cut the sentence where I talk about X". For a pass over the WHOLE video (bad takes, anything that adds nothing), a gesture this server does not offer — never this.

projectId.description: The project id (from list_projects or clone_project).

expectedRevision.description: The editRevision you last read (get_project_state, or the last write's result). If the project changed since, nothing is applied and the result is a conflict with the current revision.

confirm.description: true to confirm a mass destructive gesture (more than 3 B-rolls removed, all words restored, or more than 20 % of the remaining words cut in one call).

tools.name: restore_words
tools.description: un-cut a struck passage (✗ words)

projectId.description: The project id (from list_projects or clone_project).

expectedRevision.description: The editRevision you last read (get_project_state, or the last write's result). If the project changed since, nothing is applied and the result is a conflict with the current revision.

confirm.description: true to confirm a mass destructive gesture (more than 3 B-rolls removed, all words restored, or more than 20 % of the remaining words cut in one call).

tools.name: correct_words
tools.description: Fix the wording of ONE passage the user names (a typo, a wrong transcription). `text` carries the corrected words. For corrections touching the whole video, a gesture this server does not offer mode "correct"; for one spot, this one.

projectId.description: The project id (from list_projects or clone_project).

expectedRevision.description: The editRevision you last read (get_project_state, or the last write's result). If the project changed since, nothing is applied and the result is a conflict with the current revision.

confirm.description: true to confirm a mass destructive gesture (more than 3 B-rolls removed, all words restored, or more than 20 % of the remaining words cut in one call).

tools.name: move_passage
tools.description: Move a passage of WHOLE sentences so it plays elsewhere; nothing is cut. The hook gesture: leave beforeKey out and the passage becomes the very first thing heard, then the video goes on in its order (the greeting and intro follow it). To OPEN the video on its strongest sentence (a question, a figure, a promise), the passage IS that strong sentence and beforeKey is left out; never move the greeting or the announcement away instead. `fromKey` is the first word of the first sentence, `toKey` the last word of the last sentence (the one with the full stop), copied from the transcript. The passage must last 3 to 15 s. `beforeKey` only to place it before another sentence: the first word of that sentence. A passage that starts or ends mid-sentence is refused with the reason. This server adds `scenes`: "follow" (default) or "stay" (the B-rolls anchored on the passage keep their place in the montage). A B-roll that follows and outlasts its passage can be shortened with set_duration, or redrawn with measure_scene then insert_scene and its brollId.

projectId.description: The project id (from list_projects or clone_project).

expectedRevision.description: The editRevision you last read (get_project_state, or the last write's result). If the project changed since, nothing is applied and the result is a conflict with the current revision.

scenes.description: What happens to the B-rolls anchored on the moved words. "follow" (default): they move with their sentence; when one lasts longer than the passage, the result says so. "stay": each one keeps its moment in the montage and is re-anchored on the word said there after the move (it then plays over other words).

tools.name: set_silences
tools.description: The switch that cuts the silences (long pauses) between sentences and words across the WHOLE video. enabled:true cuts them: "coupe les blancs", "enlève les silences", "remove the pauses", "tighten the gaps". enabled:false puts them back. The project state says whether it is ON now. breathMs is the pause kept at each cut (default 300 ms, the Studio's "natural" breath); set it only when the person asks for tighter (150) or calmer (600) cuts. For a full edit the code sets the editor's breath (leadMs before speech, tailMs after, longer; minGapMs: only longer pauses are cut); change it only when asked.

projectId.description: The project id (from list_projects or clone_project).

expectedRevision.description: The editRevision you last read (get_project_state, or the last write's result). If the project changed since, nothing is applied and the result is a conflict with the current revision.

confirm.description: true to confirm a mass destructive gesture (more than 3 B-rolls removed, all words restored, or more than 20 % of the remaining words cut in one call).

tools.name: look_at_source
tools.description: SEE the raw SOURCE video at one moment: returns the picture itself (JPEG), with a 12x12 grid drawn on it (columns A-L left to right, rows 1-12 top to bottom) to help you read positions. Every zone or box you give back to the tools (add_zoom zone, a face box) is in FRACTIONS 0-1 of THIS source picture: x, y of the top-left corner, w, h of the size; one grid cell is 1/12. Also returns what the project already measured there, without a new look: the speaker's `face` box and where it comes from (an earlier look, the map of the source, the face track, or on a screen share the camera card), `sourceShows` (speaker facing the camera, screen share with a camera card, screen alone) and, on a screen share, `cameraCard`. get_scene_brief, measure_scene and insert_scene use the same face when you omit `face`. Null face: nothing measured there; read it on the picture. `at`: montage seconds, "m:ss" or a word key; source:true reads `at` as source seconds. Free; ffmpeg, under 2 s.

at.description: Montage seconds, "m:ss", or a word key.

source.description: true: `at` is in seconds of the source video.

tools.name: look_at_montage
tools.description: SEE your EDIT at one moment of the montage: renders the FINAL picture as the viewer will see it (the cut video, its zoom, every B-roll and scene on top, the speaker's card, the captions) and returns it (JPEG, 1280 px wide by default, no grid so nothing hides the face; grid: true adds the 12x12 grid), with what the code measures: the layers on screen and whether each is drawn, the speaker's face box measured before (fractions of the frame), the share of the face under each visual, the active zoom, the caption shown, and problems found. Look after placing or changing something, and before saying an edit is finished. Read-only and free; one render at a time (looks asked together wait for each other), 5 to 60 s each, so look at the moments that matter.

at.description: Montage seconds, "m:ss", or a word key.

grid.description: Draw the 12x12 grid over the picture (default false: it covers the face).

tools.name: check_edit
tools.description: Check the whole edit, by code, free, no model. Three parts. `timeline`: what gets in each other's way on the export's timeline, each with its montage seconds and a fix: two scenes on the same layer at once, a scene drawn over another, a zoom under a scene (a zoom enlarges the video, never the scene: "zoom-under-full-frame" when the render shows the scene fills the frame, so the zoom is not seen; under a transparent P9 scene, only "zoom-pushes-face-under-scene" when the zoomed face goes under the scene's elements and "zoom-shifts-scene-target" when the part of the picture the scene marks slides away), an HTML page shortened or lengthened by more than 10 % or 50 % (the export plays its whole animation faster or slower to fit its block; nothing is cut), captions drawn over a scene, a visual past the end, and "long-stretch-without-visual": every stretch of 30 s or more with no visual, with what the source shows there, where the speaker is, and `zones`: the calm bands of the picture (black bands around a shared screen, a plain wall) where a P9 scene can play, in fractions of the frame. What the cuts left behind: "visual-outside-montage" (its words cut up to the end: not shown), "visual-on-cut-words" (moved to a cut seam), "zoom-zero-length", "caption-passage-cut", each with its removal. `scenes`: every scene's pace in its block: an HTML page the export plays faster (shortened) or slower (lengthened), or a ready-made template laid out again for its block (its pace kept). `rubric`: the publish-ready rubric (hook, visual density, longest stretch without a visual, captions, retakes left, mid-sentence joins, zooms, music), what fails and how to fix it. Run it after a batch of gestures and before saying an edit is finished; then look_at_montage at the moments it names. With measure (default true) it renders one frame per scene that something overlaps, to tell a full-frame scene from a smaller one: 5 to 60 s.

measure.description: Render the frames that tell whether a scene fills the frame (default true). false: timeline only, a few seconds.

tools.name: list_zooms
tools.description: The punch-in zooms already on the video: id, scale, motion and moment (fromKey/toKey, the word keys the gestures take, and montageStartSec/montageEndSec, the seconds look_at_montage takes). Call it before update_zoom or remove_zooms; a zoom id never comes from you.

tools.name: add_zoom
tools.description: Add a punch-in zoom from startWordKey to endWordKey (or for durationSec). To show a part of the SCREEN the speaker talks about (a button, a menu, a line of code), pass `zone`: the rectangle you read on look_at_source, in fractions of the source picture; the code picks the scale and the framing that show the whole zone (the strongest allowed zoom is x1.6, so a small zone gets x1.6 centred on it, and a zone covering nearly the whole frame is refused with the reason). Without zone, give scale (1.05 to 1.6) and, only for a deliberate off-centre framing, focusX/focusY (crop-slack fractions); without them the app frames on the subject it detects. motion: snap (default), push (slow push-in), punch (hit and overshoot), keyframes (any curve or pan; not with zone). The result gives the frame actually set. A zoom enlarges the source video only, never a scene, title or image placed over it (the preview and the export do the same): under a full-frame scene it is not seen; under a transparent P9 scene the scene stays put while the face and the screen grow and slide behind it, so a mark drawn on a button no longer sits on it. check_edit names only these conflicts.

projectId.description: The project id (from list_projects or clone_project).

expectedRevision.description: The editRevision you last read (get_project_state, or the last write's result). If the project changed since, nothing is applied and the result is a conflict with the current revision.

zone.description: The zone of the screen to show WHOLE, in fractions 0-1 of the SOURCE picture as look_at_source shows it: x, y = top-left corner, w, h = size. The code computes the scale and the framing so the zoom shows all of it, never cutting a part; scale, focusX and focusY are then ignored.

focusX.description: Crop-slack fraction; only for an explicit off-centre request — otherwise omit

focusY.description: Crop-slack fraction; only for an explicit off-centre request — otherwise omit

motion.description: snap = quick zoom in, hold, out (default). push = slow build from rest to `scale` over the whole zoom (a slow push-in). punch = fast hit with a slight overshoot that settles on `scale`. keyframes = your own curve in `keyframes`.

rampInSec.description: snap/punch: zoom-in length; push: build length (default: the whole zoom)

rampOutSec.description: Release length back to rest. push defaults to 0 (ends zoomed in, like a cut)

keyframes.description: Any curve, including a PAN (move focusX/focusY between keyframes, e.g. to follow a cursor). Each keyframe: time as `p` (0..1 of the zoom) or `t` (seconds from its start), the scale there, and the easing used to ARRIVE from the previous keyframe. Start at scale 1 and end at scale 1 for a smooth in and out.

t.description: Seconds from the zoom's start (used when p is absent)

focusX.description: 0 = left edge in frame, 0.5 = centred, 1 = right edge

focusY.description: 0 = top edge in frame, 0.5 = centred, 1 = bottom edge

easing.description: linear (default), ease, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out, hold (jump at this keyframe), or "cubic-bezier(x1,y1,x2,y2)" (y above 1 overshoots)

inputSchema.description: Give endWordKey or durationSec; give scale unless you give zone.

tools.description: Remove zooms by id (from list_zooms) or all of them at once.

tools.name: list_layouts
tools.description: The scene layouts for a moment (or for the video when no moment is given): for each, whether it holds and why not (format, the speaker's face, captions), the scene box, the content box (the size of the page you write) and its background (opaque: you paint the box; transparent: P9, your elements play over the video), and the speaker card. Boxes are in px of the final frame. Free, no rendering.

toKey.description: Word key where the scene ends (inclusive).

zone.description: P9 only: the free zone where the scene's elements go, in fractions of the final frame (keep it off the face and off the screen the video shows). Default: the whole frame.

tools.name: get_scene_contract
tools.description: The technical contract of a scene page (the HTML document the app plays and exports), the base skill, every recipe and when to use it (a list said one item after another is liste-revelee), the grading grid our judge uses, and the rules of this server. Read it once before writing your first scene. `recipe` adds that recipe's full skill.

recipe.description: The recipe you follow (get_scene_contract). Default sequence-cinematique.

tools.name: get_scene_examples
tools.description: Example scene pages graded 28-29/30, one per recipe: E1 compteur-mecanique, E2 autocollants, E3 interface-simulee, E4 sequence-cinematique, E5 liste-revelee. Without `id`: the list, with the recipe of each. With `id`: its notes (LISEZMOI), the whole HTML page, and its strip (six frames of the scene, PNG) when there is one.

tools.name: get_scene_brief
tools.description: The brief of a scene, exactly what our own drawer receives: the moment and the words said, the sheet (what, where, recipe, layout, timed beats in seconds from the start of the scene), the content box (the page size you write and its background), the face, the rules the code measures in numbers for THIS frame, the canvas and the creator's preferences. `range` says whether the moment holds (its last beat before 85 % of the scene, so the last element is read) and, when it does not, the end word that makes it hold. Free; no model writes it, the code does.

toKey.description: Word key where the scene ends (inclusive).

layout.description: The layout, from list_layouts (P1 full frame, P9 transparent over the video, P2-P8/P7L/PV keep the speaker beside the scene).

tools.name: measure_scene
tools.description: Try a scene page without writing anything: the code checks the page (structure, network, GSAP plugins, selectors, script syntax; a refusal lists the problems), places it in its layout over the real video, films it in Chrome and measures it like our chain does: broken or not and why (frozen, empty, cut text, placeholder frame, face covered, nothing new on a beat), plus notes to improve it. Returns the strip of the scene on the video and the content box alone. No judge and no model: you judge the pictures. Free: no credit, no model, a Chrome render of 20 to 90 s, one at a time. A scene usually takes 2 or 3 measures (fix everything a measure lists before the next), and a full edit draws several scenes: the cap of 12 measures per scene per hour is a ceiling against loops, not a cost.

tools.name: insert_scene
tools.description: Place your scene in the montage: the page is checked and measured as measure_scene does (the measure is reused when the same page was just measured), then the B-roll and its page are written together, so the app plays and exports it without drawing anything. Status: ready (measured by code, not judged) when not broken, to review when broken. `brollId` replaces that scene (it gets a new id). Returns the new brollId and the editRevision, and `soundEffects`: the effects the code planned from the page itself (a whoosh on the scene's entrance, a click or a pop on its elements, as our own chain does); list_sfx shows them, remove_sfx takes them out. Free.

tools.name: get_scene
tools.description: Read a scene: its moment (fromKey, toKey, montage start and end seconds, duration, layer), what kind of page it is (an HTML page, or a ready-made template: title, versus, big number, quote, checklist), the text it shows (a template's `texts`, each with its field, or the visible text of a page) and whether that text's language matches the video's, and for a scene of the app's scene chain its layout, status, grade, the reasons that broke it and the code's measures. `html: true` adds the stored page (the one played and exported). To change a scene: set_scene_text for a template's words, set_duration for its length, move_broll to re-anchor it on its words, set_broll_pip for the speaker's window; to change how it looks, write a new page and replace it in place with measure_scene then insert_scene with its brollId and the fromKey/toKey given here. Free.

html.description: Also return the stored page of an HTML scene.

tools.name: set_scene_text
tools.description: Change the words of a ready-made template scene (title, versus, big number, quote, checklist) in place: `texts` maps each field get_scene lists under `texts` ("title", "items.2", "leftLabel"…) to its new text. Only existing text fields change; the scene keeps its look, moment and length, and the app draws it again from the new words. Use it to put a scene in the video's language, fix a wording, or match what the speaker says. A scene with an HTML page has no fields: redraw it instead (measure_scene, then insert_scene with its brollId). Free.

Composed by code as a transparent P9 scene over the video: no drawing, no film, instant and free. A zoom on the same words moves the picture under the mark: keep zooms off it (check_edit says so). Replace or remove it like any scene (remove_brolls).

When the user names no length, a longer one you choose that still ends before the sentence the visual illustrates is lengthened to that sentence, up to the limit of its place; the result says so. On a visual this request did not create, only when the request names a length. On this server the result gives each scene's `pace`: an HTML page is never cut, the export plays its whole animation faster when you shorten it ("plays 2.1 times faster") and slower when you lengthen it; to keep its pace, redraw it for the new length (measure_scene then insert_scene with its brollId). A ready-made template is laid out again for its new length and keeps its pace.

tools.name: set_broll_pip
tools.description: Show the speaker in a window ON TOP of a B-roll (the "pop-out"; it changes the picture, not the sound). `enabled: false` turns it off. Without position or box, the code renders the scene, finds the box it keeps empty for the camera (the "empty-box" problem look_at_montage reports) and puts the window ON that box, at its size, framed on the speaker's face: 5 to 60 s. A scene with no such box gets the default corner, and the result says so. `box`: a free rectangle in % of the frame, for a place of your choice. `position`: a named corner (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right, center), only when the creator asks for a corner. `size` (window width in %) only goes with position. Free.

box.description: A free rectangle for the window, in % of the frame: x, y = top-left corner, w, h = size (as look_at_montage reports a box, e.g. x 56-84 %, y 39-67 % is x 56, y 39, w 28, h 28). The window fills it at its shape, framed on the speaker's face.

tools.name: apply_layout
tools.description: Put a scene of the scene chain (one you drew with insert_scene, or one the app drew) in another layout, by code: free, instant, nothing redrawn, the same path as the Studio's Layouts panel. The scene is placed in its new box; a layout that keeps the speaker beside it frames the face (on a screen share, inside the camera card). A layout that does not hold is refused with the reason and the layouts that hold (list_layouts gives them for a moment). A background check films the result and marks it "needs a fit" when it sits badly; look_at_montage at the scene to judge it. A ready-made template is not a chain scene: redraw it with insert_scene and its brollId.

tools.name: get_captions
tools.description: Read the project's subtitle track: whether it is on, whether it covers the whole video or chosen passages (each with its word keys, montage start and end in seconds, and words), its style (catalogue look, preset, position, size, colours, words per line), `styleBy` (whether the creator chose it) and the creator's default style when the account has one, and `catalogue`: the styles set_captions takes in `style` (id, English and French names, family). Free. Change it with set_captions (whole video, chosen passages in `ranges`, a catalogue `style`) or add_caption (one passage).

tools.name: set_captions
tools.description:
Turn the project's subtitle track on or off. When on, every spoken word of the montage is captioned (2 lines max, cut words skipped, the word being spoken highlighted) and burned into the export. This is the tool for subtitles on the WHOLE video, when the user asks for that ("captions on the whole video", "sous-titres sur toute la vidéo"). One call covers the whole video: no word keys. A full edit does not turn it on unless asked: it places subtitles on a few key passages with add_caption. `preset`: bold (default, big uppercase, highlighted word), karaoke (coloured active word), clean (plain white), minimal (small, on a dark box). `position` bottom|middle|top. The style is set here too, when the user asks: `color` is the text colour (#rrggbb, or yellow, white, red, green, blue, orange, pink, purple, cyan, black; French names too), `highlightColor` the colour of the word being spoken (never the text colour: it would not show, so the code switches it to white, or yellow on white text), `sizePct` the size in % of the frame's short side (clean 5, bold 6.5; "bigger" is 8 to 10, max 12). A preset resets the style, so send the colour and size in the same call as the preset. `highlight` and `maxWordsPerLine` only when the user asks. enabled:false removes them. `style` puts a whole look from the subtitle catalogue at once (font, colours, spoken word, box, animation), by name; the position, a size the creator set and the passages stay. When the creator chose the style (on the track, or as their default), keep it: no style, preset or colours unless they ask for a new look. When they have not, a full edit picks the style that suits the video.

Through this server: get_captions lists the catalogue styles (`catalogue`: id, French and English names, family) for `style`. The answer reads back the track as written: each passage with its keys, montage start and end in seconds and its words, and the style it wears. When the creator chose the subtitle style (styleBy creator, or a default style on the account), style, preset and colours are left out unless you pass lookAsked: true because the creator asked to change their look.

tools.name: add_caption
tools.description: Put subtitles on ONE short passage: the words where the speaker puts the emphasis (the hook, a key figure, the punchline, a strong statement), a few words, under 8 s. The passage joins the subtitled passages of the project's subtitle track; call it once per passage, several in the same turn: each call adds one and keeps the others. This is how a full edit places its subtitles, spread over the video. Keys come from the transcript, never from you. `layout` and `align` only when the user asks for a style. Subtitles on the whole video only when the user asks for them in so many words ("subtitles on the whole video", "sous-titres partout"): that is set_captions, never a long add_caption.

tools.name: list_music
tools.description: The background music tracks available: id and title. Call it before set_music; a track id never comes from you. Says which track the project plays today, if any.

tools.name: set_music
tools.description: Set the background music from the library (the track id comes from list_music) over the whole video, or clear it with trackId: null. Without `volume`, the level starts where the app's mixer starts: computed from the track's loudness so the music sits under the voice. `level` chooses: "recommended" sets that starting level (and the mixer's ducking and fades), even on the track already placed; "keep" keeps the level of the music in place, even for another track; without it, a different track starts at the recommended level and the same track keeps its settings. The answer says which applied: given, recommended or kept. check_audio then says how loud the music sits under the voice and in the pauses. `volume` 0 to 1 sets it by hand. `ducking` (default true) lowers the music while the speaker talks; `duck` picks how much: subtle (8 dB, the default), normal (12 dB) or strong (18 dB). `fadeInSec` and `fadeOutSec` (default 1 s and 3 s, 0 to 10). It replaces the music already placed, all its pieces. Free.

trackId.description: A library id from list_music, or null to remove the music.

level.description: recommended: the mixer's starting level for this track, even when it is already placed; keep: the level of the music in place, even for another track. Ignored when volume is given.

duck.description: How much the music lowers under the voice: subtle (8 dB), normal (12 dB), strong (18 dB).

tools.name: list_sfx
tools.description: The sound-effect library and the effects placed. `library`: each sound's id, name, category and length; `roles`: the role names add_sfx also takes (whoosh, pop, click, impact, typing…) and the sound each plays. `placed`: for each visual that carries effects, its id, its moment and each effect with its index (for remove_sfx), sound and montage second. In this app an effect rides on a visual (a scene, an image, a clip): it plays at a moment of that visual. Free.

tools.name: add_sfx
tools.description: Add one sound effect at a moment: `at` is a word key or montage seconds, `sound` a role (whoosh, pop, click, impact, rise, ding, typing…) or a library id from list_sfx. The effect rides on the visual on screen at that moment (the top one, or `brollId`); the effects already there stay. No visual there: refused, because an effect plays with a visual in this app; draw a scene there first. `volume` 0 to 1 (default: the library's level). Free.

at.description: Montage seconds, "m:ss", or a word key.

sound.description: A role or a library id (list_sfx).

brollId.description: The visual to put it on; default: the top visual on screen at `at`.

tools.name: remove_sfx
tools.description: Remove sound effects from a visual: `index` (from list_sfx `placed`) removes one, `all: true` silences the visual. The others stay. Free.

tools.name: check_audio
tools.description: Hear the mix, by code: the voice's level measured on spoken passages of the source, then, in dB AGAINST THE VOICE, each music track in the pauses and under the voice (after its duck), with a verdict, and the sound effects whose peak jumps over the voice or that sit less than 0.5 s apart (the ear hears one). Two readings: `preview` (the voice as recorded) and `export` (with the export's volume option on, the voice alone is brought to -14 LUFS; music and effects stay where the mixer set them). Music sits well about 15 to 25 dB under the voice. Free: no model, no credit.
